# Wiki Conventions

How pages link to each other, and when the engines check those links.

**See also:** `wiki-federation-model` — for the structural and ownership model: the three-layer storage model, federation map, origination trust modes, and authorship hedges.
**See also:** `wiki-page-placement` — for where a page may sit and what it may depend on.
**See also:** `wiki-scaffold-files` — for the files every sub-wiki contains.
**See also:** `wiki-page-content-rules` — for callouts, code citations and product-page wording.

## Authorship boundary

The skills that write pages each own a write-set; every other wiki skill is read-only against pages. Lint and the conformance audit write only their report, to the report directory (`wiki-configuration`).

`wiki-write-protocol` names each skill's write-set.

## Cross-reference protocol

Every cross-reference is a wiki-link. `/wiki-lint` validates resolution when it is run.

- **Syntax:** `[[<domain>:<path>#<anchor>]]` — e.g. `[[governance:roadmap/2026-q3#commitments]]`.
- **Intra-wiki shorthand:** within the same sub-wiki may omit the domain prefix — `[[entities/cart]]`. Cross-wiki links MUST include it.
- **Resolution:** `<wiki.location>/<domain>/<path>.md`.
- **Anchors:** an anchor is the slug of a heading's whole text in the target page. To derive it, lowercase the heading; drop every character other than an ASCII letter, digit, `_`, space or `-`; turn each space into `-` without collapsing runs; and trim a leading or trailing `-`. Inline code keeps its text, slugged like the rest of the heading. A heading whose slug repeats an earlier heading's on the same page takes `-1`, the next repeat `-2`. Compute an anchor with `node .agent-kit/dist/wiki/scripts/wiki-slug.js --anchor "<heading>"` rather than by hand; the **Anchor examples** after this list show the rule at work.
- **Raw / archive references:** `[[_raw:<path>]]`, `[[_archive:<path>]]`.
- **Lint:** a broken cross-wiki link is a `/wiki-lint` error.
- **Regression:** a page that loses its last inbound reference in a diff is a `/wiki-conformance-audit` warning naming the orphaned page — the hand-unlinking gap the wiki's move step, which validates before writing, does not cover. A `redirect` stub is exempt; that IS the archival path.
- **Hierarchy:** must respect the reference hierarchy from `wiki-federation-model`, for both `related:` lists and body `[[...]]` links. `/wiki-lint` Pass 2 reports violations as errors.
- **Ordering:** `related:` lists and `## Related …` body sections are ordered — `wiki-authoring-spec` §Authoring for readability is canonical.

**Anchor examples** — the anchor `wiki-slug.js --anchor` prints for each heading:

| Heading | Anchor |
|---|---|
| `Users — create account (create form)` | `users--create-account-create-form` |
| `Run detail (detail)` | `run-detail-detail` |
| ``Edit `config.json` (form)`` | `edit-configjson-form` |
| `API Design & Patterns` | `api-design--patterns` |


**When the rules are enforced.** `/wiki-lint` and `/wiki-conformance-audit` are CLIs a person or an agent runs — before a PR, after a redeploy, or on a cadence — and neither is wired to a commit hook, so a violation lands and is reported at the next run; a project that wants the stronger guarantee wires the CLI into its own pre-commit hook or CI job.
